items.synopsis: PTX10k2-36QDD showing incorrect Power Status
items.description: On a PTX10k2-36QDD system, the output of "show chassis environment" may incorrectly shows a disconnected PEM's status as "OK" instead of "Check".

items.synopsis: The interface fails to come up after FPC reboot if the streaming server and export profile are not configured correctly
items.description: On all Junos and Junos evolved platforms with telemetry enabled, if the streaming server and export profile for reporting-rate are not properly configured in the analytics settings, rebooting the FPC would prevent any of the interfaces from coming up.

items.synopsis: Link flapping occurs on stable subinterfaces when using QDD400GZR optics if any one subinterface in the channelized group is down
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms that support the QDD-400G-ZR coherent optical transceiver modules (400G-ZR and 400G OpenZR+), when an interface is equipped with any of these optics and configured in breakout mode, if anyone of the sub-interfaces in the group is administratively up and operationally down, the remaining stable sub-interfaces in the same group experience the link flaps at a regular interval.

items.category: the replication daemon (repd) for Shared Memory-base
items.synopsis: RPD might crash when upgrading using no-validate.
items.description: RPD might crash when upgrading and NOT using no-validate. Use no-validate to avoid the crash.

items.synopsis: Configuring max color value 2^32-1(4294967295) in transport-class does not create the corresponding transport-class color table
items.description: On device configured with LSP with transport-class, when configuring max color value (2^32-1=4294967295), transport-class color table is not created and rpd may core. This issue only happens with configuring the max color value.

items.synopsis: Updating a source-file to load ROAs should be done by changing the name of the source file
items.description: Loading ROAs from a source-file was a feature introduced as a convenience feature and as such this only affects that feature. This feature is not in widespread use and was created to have a fallback ROA when all sessions go down. This problem scenario requires multiple reloads with the being modified back and forth to add and then delete and re-add the database configured in the import policy.

items.synopsis: Memory leak is observed when "graceful-shutdown" is configured
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) "graceful-shutdown" configured, memory leak is observed. This issue does not cause traffic impact.

items.synopsis: Valid BGP routes in RIB are displayed with verification state as Invalid
items.description: On Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, with resource public key infrastructure(RPKI ) enabled for the BGP, the valid routes are installed in the routing table with validation state invalid.However, the route is parsed by policy as a valid route.

items.synopsis: BGP updates missing graceful-shutdown community after quick sender knob flaps
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when the graceful-shutdown sender knob is repeatedly deleted and subsequently re-added in quick intervals under a BGP-LU (Border Gateway Protocol-Labeled Unicast) session, the router CLI (command line interface) incorrectly indicates that the graceful-shutdown community is being advertised. However, the actual BGP update messages sent over the session do not include the graceful-shutdown community. This results in the graceful-shutdown community not being propagated to BGP peers during graceful shutdown events, which will potentially cause traffic forwarding issues.

items.synopsis: rpd crash when changes are applied to as-path with dynamic-db in use
items.description: On Junos OS platforms using as-path-groups (Autonomous System Path Group) with dynamic-db (dynamic Data base) feature enabled, rpd (Routing Protocol Daemon) may crash after as-path configuration changes.

items.synopsis: EBGP MULTIPATH is not set on ACTIVE route
items.description: On all Junos/EVO platforms, in BGP multipath scenario, it is observed that due to a software issue, the Active route does not have all the ECMP legs. Hence only one leg is installed to forwarding.

items.category: PFE COS features on BT based platforms
items.synopsis: Rare evo-cda-bt crash in PTX10008 Junos OS Evolved with multiple FPCs when one FPC fails
items.description: On all Junos Evolved PTX10008 platforms, the failure of one FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) can cause a rare evo-cda-bt crash on another FPC, resulting in a reboot.

items.synopsis: MIB2D will see 100% CPU utilization due to MIB2D walk fail
items.description: On PTX3000/PTX5000/PTX10008 /PTX10016/QFX10008 /PTX1000/PTX10002/ QFX10002 platforms, MIB2D will see 100% CPU utilization due to MIB2D walk failure.

items.synopsis: System becomes unresponsive or crash due to frequent filter changes in a scale scenario having mib2d process in use
items.description: On Junos OS platforms, The system experiences memory exhaustion due to an mbuf (Memory Buffer) leak, system logs error message. This condition can cause the system to become unresponsive (hang state) or potentially crash, resulting in a VMcore file and service disruption. The issue arises when a firewall filter is applied to approximately 1k (1000) logical interfaces (IFLs), each filter containing over 250 terms and these filters are updated every 2-3 minutes, triggering updates for all filter attachments.

items.synopsis: Traffic disruption is observed when successive switchover is performed having single-hop BFD configured in the dual RE scenario
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7509, ACX7332, ACX7348 platforms with dual RE, protocol flap is observed when BFD (Bidirectional Forwarding Detection) liveness detection fails, leading to traffic disruption. This issue occurs because the Backup Routing Engine (RE), which takes over as the Master after successive RE switchover, has an incomplete or missing BFD session state. As a result, upon becoming the Master, it is unable to maintain established BFD sessions, triggering routing protocol reconvergence and causing temporary traffic interruption.

items.synopsis: Commit can fail if apply-path contains pattern-matching tokens other than the wildcard <*>
items.description: When the apply-path contains pattern-matching tokens other than the wildcard < >, prefix list validation may fail, causing the commit to fail.

items.synopsis: Matching TOS IP precedence values in the same term by firewall family inet on ACX 7100 and all ACX evo
items.description: Firewall filter IP precedence match incorrect when a range of values is configured. With matching only one precedence value, either (6 or 7) as an example, packets match the correct term and the action is achieved. Or when configuring a firewall family filter to match the precedence value, for example, of internet-control (6) and net-control (7) in the same term, packets do not match the correct term, and the action is not achieved.

items.category: Host path software for ACX platform
items.synopsis: The Devdb messages will be seen continuously on ACX EVO platforms
items.description: On ACX EVO platforms, due to the Discard filter programmed and the traffic hitting continuously on the same discard filter, the Devdb messages continuously keeps flooded.

items.synopsis: Packet loss or retransmissions observed on MX platforms using SFP-T transceivers
items.description: On MX10004, MX10008 and MX10016 platforms with LC480 line cards, the use of Small Form-factor Pluggable Twisted-pair (SFP-T) transceiver will lead to packet loss or retransmissions on neighboring devices due to incorrect Inter-Packet Gap (IPG) handling.

items.synopsis: SNMP walk failure due to missing OID after FCO/TPA delete compression
items.description: On all PTX Junos and Junos evolved platforms, an issue occurs when performing SNMP walks, resulting in the error No Such Instance currently exists at this OID. This is caused by a lifecycle management problem involving FCO (Factory Configuration Object) and TPA (Third-Party Attachment) objects. Specifically, when both FCO (IFDO) and TPA (IfSnmpInfo) are deleted in quick succession, only the FCO delete notification is sent, skipping the FCO modification callback that the TPA would typically trigger a delete event. As a result, the SNMP index mapping associated with the TPA is not properly updated, leading to missing entries during SNMP walks.

items.category: Issues related to EVO dependency layer including object graphs, incompletes, anomalies and nkdb
items.synopsis: Rare assert with an Junos Evolved process
items.description: This is a rare chance of a process panic. This can be seen in Evo apps. If seen in forwarding apps it can result in system reboot and resulting traffic loss.

items.category: System Management daemon and related issues
items.synopsis: System stops responding to "show system applications app ndp detail" command or prevents applications from start/stop/restart
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, a failure in internal process communication will cause the system to stop responding to the "show system applications app ndp detail" CLI command or prevent applications from start/stop/restart. This issue occurs when systemd becomes unresponsive to requests initiated by sysman. There is no impact to traffic forwarding.

items.synopsis: Disabling a single AE IFL in a MAC-VRF can bring the entire AE interface down
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, under MAC-VRF routing configurations, when any Layer 3 IFL is deactivated, it causes the associated AE interface to go administratively down, leading to complete traffic disruption across the AE bundle.

items.synopsis: Interface remains administratively down state, fails to recover after execution of CLI command "request interface bounce"
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX platforms, executing the CLI command "request interface bounce" causes the member Ethernet interface (et-x/x/x), which is part of the Aggregated Ethernet (AE) bundle, to remain in an administratively down state and not recover after the defined interval. As a result, this condition can cause a traffic impact.

items.synopsis: AE interface speed mismatch causes link down and missing command outputs on Junos OS Evolved platforms
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, when the AE (Aggregated Ethernet) interface is configured with a link-speed different from its member interfaces, it results in a misconfiguration. Due to this, the link between devices goes down, causing disruption in traffic forwarding.

items.category: EVO Netstack Juniper Tunnel Driver Module
items.synopsis: TCP connection stalls with BGP Explicit Null and MPLS forwarding on certain Junos Evolved PTX platforms when sending packets exceeding MTU limit
items.description: On Junos Evolved PTX10001, PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms, if LDP(Label Distribution Protocol) is initially established over IP protocol, and later transitions to MPLS(Multiprotocol Label Switching) encapsulation (mpls-forwarding), the outgoing TCP(Transmission Control Protocol) packet size is not adjusted to account for added MPLS label. As a result, packets exceeding the configured interface MTU(Maximum Transmission Unit) are dropped before transmission. Since the receiving side does not receive these packets, the LDP session eventually times out due to "hold time expiry".

items.synopsis: Transient traffic loss for CE in an EVPN MPLS setup with Multi-Homing
items.description: On Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with EVPN MPLS, Multi-Homing scenarios, when there is a Multi-Homing peer node reboot, the destination route entries that were learned locally on IRB(Integrated Routing and Bridging) interface of rebooted node get deleted on other multi-homing peers without RE-ARP (Routing Engine-Address Resolution Protocol) causing transient traffic loss for CE (Customer Edge) traffic.

items.synopsis: PTX10001-36MR reboot after ppman-aft-bt hot patch.
items.description: Hot patch and restart of ppman-aft-bt will cause a reboot of the system. This is specific to PTX10001-36MR and 23.4.

items.category: Express PFE MPLS for EVO platforms
items.synopsis: Control plane is not properly managing the label 1048575 for MPLS traffic, leading to service impact
items.description: On PTX Evolved platforms, the control plane is incorrectly using label 1048575 for MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) traffic, this label is being changed to the NULL label 3, as if it corresponds to a non-MPLS packet, resulting in the label being popped, leading to all traffic associated to these MPLS threads to be dropped.

items.synopsis: Traffic drop occurs on Junos Evolved platforms when prefix is moved between dynamic prefix-lists used in firewall filter
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, when a firewall filter is configured with a dynamic prefix-list that is referenced using an apply-path statement, moving a prefix from one such prefix-list to another where both prefix-lists match the apply-path pattern results in the prefix not being programmed in the PFE. This causes traffic loss for that prefix. The issue is triggered when the configuration includes apply-path pointing to both the source and destination prefix-lists, and a prefix is deleted from one and added to the other through a commit operation.

items.synopsis: The data plane will be out of sync when migrating to EVPN A/A stitching with Vanila VXLAN (PIM Multicast)
items.description: On MX platforms, to improve the convergence of node failures in EVPN MH interconnects with Data Plane VXLAN, migrating to an Active-Active setup may cause the data plane to become out of sync for ARP entries. The gateway learns the MAC address and advertises it to the peer gateway. However, on the peer gateway, some MAC-IP entries may remain stuck in the 'Unresolved' (Ur) state.

items.synopsis: NPU's (Network Processing Unit) KHT (Kernal Hash Table) utilization shows 100% utilization post config commit
items.description: On Junos Evolved platforms, NPU's KHT utilization shows 100% utilization post config commit

items.synopsis: On ACX7348 and ACX7332 , Jack Out Jack In of FPC blocks MACSEC traffic
items.description: On ACX7348 and ACX7332 Junos Evolved Platforms during Jack out of FPC, MACSEC resources are not properly cleaned up, this results in initialisation failure and MACSEC traffic getting blocked after FPC is Jacked In.

items.synopsis: Interface down is observed while configuring 1G speed on ACX7332/ACX7348/ACX7509 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX7332/ACX7348/ACX7509 platforms, physical interface goes down on configuring 1G speed after the first boot with or without auto-negotiation.

items.synopsis: ACX7024 sees a vmcore and restarts or potentially hangs on reboot
items.description: ACX7024 sees a vmcore and restarts or potentially hangs on reboot

items.synopsis: Evo-pfemand process crashes on ACX7348/ACX7332/ACX7024/ACX7509 platforms
items.description: On ACX7348/ACX7332/ACX7024/ACX7509 platforms, evo-pfemand process crashes after evo-pfemand application restarts or after a RE(Routing Engine) switchover resulting in impact on forwarding traffic.

items.synopsis: Link State of IS-IS IPv6 adjacency is not updated after interface flap (Due to any reason)
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with Intermediate System-to-Intermediate System (IS-IS) protocol configured with IPv6 Multitopology, in rare scenarios the IS-IS adjacency is not updated and IPv6 traffic drop is seen after restarting the FPC.

items.synopsis: The l2ald crash is observed when adding scaled EVPN-VXLAN configuration on Junos platforms
items.description: On Junos platforms, if disk is full, when scaling configuration is moved to baseline configuration and move back to scaling configuration, l2ald try to create a source VTEP, but old VTEP is still in the middle of deletion, so kernel return EBUSY and l2ald will retry. If retry too many times, l2ald insist and core.

items.synopsis: High FPC CPU utilisation and local MAC learning failure in EVPN-MPLS scenario due to rapid MAC moves
items.description: On all Junos platforms (except MX platforms with MPC10, MPC11, LC9600) with Ethernet Virtual Private Network (VPN) - Multiprotocol Label Switching (EVPN-MPLS) configured, Media Access Control (MAC) learning failure and high CPU utilisation in FPC is seen due to rapid MAC moves and incorrect interface state in Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE).

items.synopsis: AE member not able to discover lost LACP peer connection leading to traffic black-holing
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when a loop occurs in the transmission switch, the device starts receiving looped LACP (Link Aggregation Control Protocol) PDU's from itself, instead of messages from the actual peer device. This causes the system to mistakenly believe that a valid LACP connection exists, even though the peer device is not actually connected.As a result, it continues to forward traffic as if the peer were active. Since no valid peer connection is present, this can lead to traffic blackholing .

items.synopsis: The authd process crashes when /etc/resolv.conf file is empty
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved ACX platforms, when DHCP (Dynamic Host Control Protocol) local server is configured without domain-name specified, the authd process crash may be observed. There will be no forwarding traffic impact due this issue, however, new DHCP client requests will not be answered.

items.category: MPC11 ULC platform software related issues.
items.synopsis: MX2010: MPC11E - FPC 1 temp sensor DDR4 A failed
items.description: DDR temp sensor is designed to be used periodically to get temps to send to chassisd. The temp sensors reside may have an intermittent contention that can cause these read failures resulting in DDR4 Temp Sensor Fail" logs on MPC11E linecards.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes due to memory exhaustion
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, an out-of-memory condition in the rpd process caused by uncontrolled memory allocation leads to the rpd process crashing.

items.synopsis: RSVP-TE LSP path is not re-optimised to the path with best IGP metric
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when RSVP-TE (Resource Reservation Protocol - Traffic Engineering) is configured with MBB (make-before-break) setup, if the protected link of the primary LSP (Label Switched Path) goes down and if "clear mpls lsp" or "clear rsvp session" commands are executed, then LSP switches to new instance from the old which will be on higher IGP (Interior Gateway Protocol) metric. However, after re-optimization, LSP will not get switched to better IGP metric path and remain in old instance. Traffic drop can be seen due to this double fault events.

items.synopsis: MX960 mcsnoopd core dump during rt_mcnh_nh_release
items.description: The root cause is, when the system comes up after reboot, in MCSNOOPD (/usr/sbin/mcsnoopd used for L2 multicast), the lsi interfaces are learned. In MCSNOOPD, when there are 4 lsi interfaces learned, we create a nexthop(assume VE NH1) with all these 4 lsi as members and we use it in the routes for forwarding the traffic. When MCSNOOPD learns 5th lsi interface, as per internal NH(nexthop) allocation logic, we allocate a new nh(assume VE NH2) containing all these 5 lsi interfaces and free the old NH(VE NH1). The old freed NH(VE NH1) is accessed and tried to be freed again in another part of the code flow which is causing MCSNOOPD core(/usr/sbin/mcsnoopd). The fix is to free the old NH(VE NH1) in a common place instead of freeing in multiple places.

items.synopsis: PIM neighbors timeout on backup RE due to inconsistent state with master
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms with dual Routing Engines (REs), Protocol Independent Multicast (PIM) neighborship is not be maintained on the backup Routing Engine after a ppmd-agent restart. This can lead to loss of PIM neighbor state on the backup RE.

items.synopsis: Wrong digest algorithm is used for ECDSA key based certificate requests using PKI
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, when generating Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm (ECDSA) based Certificate Signing Request (CSR) using Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), SHA-384 digest is used even when other digest algorithm is specified in Command Line Interface (CLI). This issue will impact services that are based on these certificates when the services are configured for specific digest algorithm.

items.synopsis: QFX5700: SFP+-10G-ACU1M : DAC Cable port down on after performing jack out and jack in.
items.description: QFX5700: SFP+-10G-ACU1M : DAC Cable port down on after performing jack out and jack in. This issue will not be seen if the recommended procedure for cable jack-out and jack-in is followed: 1. Disable the interface from EVO configuration 2. Jack-out the cable 3. Jack-in the cable (or another cable) 4. Re-enable the interface from the EVO configuration If the recommended procedure is not followed, and a jack-out/jack-in is performed, this issue will be hit. To come out of this situation, the workaround is to disable and re-enable the affected interface from EVO configuration.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes and asserts are seen due to memory leak
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, rpd process crashes and asserts are seen due to a memory leak when BGP sharding is enabled and 'show route' is performed continuously.

items.category: RPD Next-hop issues including indirect, CNH, and MCNH
items.synopsis: Route change is not synced after rpd restart due to rib-fib inconsistency
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, after rpd (Routing Protocol Daemon) restart, the route change is not sent from routing daemon RIB(Routing Information Base) to forwarding plane FIB (Forwarding Information Base). This results in traffic drop.

items.category: RPD route tables, resolver, routing instances, static routes
items.synopsis: BGP queue deadlock on Junos/Junos OS Evolved/cRPD platforms leading to route advertisement failure and traffic loss
items.description: On all Junos, Junos OS Evolved, and cRPD platforms, due to deadlock in internal processes, BGP (Border Gateway Protocol) route advertisement fails leading to traffic disruption.

items.category: Bug and Review Tracking for Segment routing traffic eng
items.synopsis: A momentary drop in traffic is observed when changes are applied on multipath SR-TE LSPs
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS EVO (Evolved) platforms, when using SR-TE (Segment Routing-Traffic Engineering) LSP (Label-Switched Path) within a multipath container, a configuration or state change (Eg: modifying the maximum-ecmp value) or a change to the segment-list on one SR-TE LSP, may impact other LSP traffic which are pointing to the same BGP Protocol next-hop. During such event, SR-TE routes are temporarily moved to a hidden state, leading to brief traffic disruption. This occurs because SR-TE is populating route parameters with an unusable next-hop.

items.category: Configuration mgmt, ffp, load-action, commit processing
items.synopsis: The commit error is seen in backup RE on MX platforms
items.description: On all MX platforms, the commit fails in Backup RE during configuration commit where "fast-synchronise" and "graceful-switchover" are being committed together.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: Command line freezes when Ctrl+Z is used
items.description: In Junos OS Releases 24.2 and later(BSD 15), pressing Ctrl+Z in the Command Line Interface CLI suspends the process and causes it to become unresponsive. This behaviour is observed on systems using the and Berkeley Software Distribution BSD15 platform.

items.category: UI Infrastructure - mgd, DAX API, DDL/ODL
items.synopsis: The dcd process crashes when deactivating only 'swap' under ' interfaces <> unit <> output-vlan-map' with no other attributes present
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, this issue affects configurations where Virtual Local Area Network (VLAN) mapping is used, particularly in scenarios where only the swap attribute is applied under 'interfaces <> unit <> output-vlan-map'. Sequence of 'Deactivate -> Activate -> Commit' of the config hieararchy leads to crash of the device control daemon (dcd) process, potentially causing service disruption.

items.category: Issues related to Logging/Tracing, errmsg, eventd infrastruc
items.synopsis: TCP session between syslog server and device remains in closed state
items.description: On all Junos platforms, a TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) connection issue occurs between the device and syslog server after an idle period exceeding 2 hours. The session gets terminated and remains in a closed state without initiating any new session until the syslog server configuration is deleted and added again. This impacts disruption in log forwarding to the remote syslog server.

items.synopsis: Performance measurement will be impacted on deactivating both chassis and PTP configuration and power off USB
items.description: On ACX7024 Junos OS Evolved platform, performance measurement impact will be seen (measurement will be incorrect since compensation removed) on deactivating both chassis and PTP configuration and power off USB. It is very unlikely sequence to be happened.

items.synopsis: A traffic outage is seen when disabling and enabling the LACP configuration
items.description: On all Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms that support EVPN Egress Link Protection, the AE(Aggregated Ethernet) member-link "Device flags" keeps "Present Running PFE-Gone" even after the LACP(Link Aggregation Control Protocol) configuration is re-enabled.

items.synopsis: PTP packets which are incoming with with padded bytes are dropped on certain Junos Evolved ACX platforms
items.description: In a rare scenario, on Junos Evolved ACX7024, ACX7100-32C and ACX7100-48L platforms configured with PTP (Precision Time Protocol) it is observed that the PTP FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) drops the incoming PTP packets with trailing padded bytes. But there is no impact to the active traffic due to this issue, apart from the PTP traffic (PTP is impacted since Delay-Request/Response packets are getting dropped).

items.synopsis: ACX7024 see's a "\" character in show chassis hardware output
items.description: Whenever the USB device brand Rally2 is connected to USB port A, a stale /dev/sda entry is being created, which results in junk characters being printed in the show chassis hardware output. To address this issue a fix has been added to verify whether the opened device is a valid block device. If it's not, the code now skips to the next iteration without processing it. Added logic to sanitize the device string by replacing junk characters with spaces. Introduced additional checks to validate block count and size, preventing further processing of dummy or invalid devices.

items.synopsis: MTU configuration is not applied from the configuration group after commit and "warning" is seen
items.description: When configuring MTU on interfaces through a configuration-group and commit the changes, those are not saved on the configuration file.

items.synopsis: ACX EVO - FTP "file copy" causing BFD flaps
items.description: Multihop sessions in ACX are distributed sessions(software-based) and not inlined (hardware-offloaded). Distributed sessions are hosted by the ppman application, that shares the same CPU with rest of the JunosE applications. During the time of copy, packetio is used considerably which would have delayed in processing other control packets. Since the BFD sessions were running at a detection-time of 300ms, a delay in packetio path to ppman could influence the timer expiry, if ppman does not receive enough packet within the detection-time. For improved failure detection, BFD is configured on all BGP sessions using a 300ms detection timer (100x3). BGP BFD can be singlehop or multihop sessions, while singlehop bfd sessions support this interval, multihop bfd does not. Multihop sessions on ACX7348, ACX7024, ACX7100, do not support BFD 3x100ms, use 3x1000ms

items.synopsis: The router incorrectly assume the VRRP Master role on Junos Evolved ACX platforms
items.description: On Junos Evolved ACX platforms, dual VRRP mastership may be seen with VRRP configuration and having filter configuration with log/syslog action. Due to the issue, the VRRP advertisements were not processed correctly, it was receiving the advertisements but getting discarded when log action is configured on the filter, so it assumed the master role. The issue may affect traffic using VRRP protocol.

items.synopsis: VSTP convergence failure on Junos OS Evolved ACX7K when IRB shares bridge domain with VSTP enabled IFL
items.description: On all Junos Evolved ACX7K platforms, when a VLAN Spanning Tree Protocol (VSTP) enabled Layer 2 logical interface (IFL) shares a bridge domain with an Integrated Routing and Bridging (IRB) interface, VSTP fails to converge due to Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) packets are misrouted to the IRB interface, preventing them from reaching the VSTP process. This causes potential traffic loops due to lack of VSTP convergence.

items.synopsis: The firewalld process crashes post specific set of filter related modifications performed in single commit
items.description: On Junos EVO platforms, When Firewall Filter change involved both delete and change to new filter on an interface in a single commit resulted in Firewalld coredump

items.synopsis: Interfaces with the same outer VLAN ID but different inner vlans or inner-lists/ranges are reporting a commit error
items.description: On all Junos OS Evolved platforms, When an interface configured with the same outer VLAN ID but with different inner vlans or inner-lists/ranges, reports a commit error.

items.category: EVO Netstack Juniper Tunnel Driver Module
items.synopsis: Memory leak is observed when Telemetry is configured
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms having Telemetry configured, the memory allocations in 512 bytes slab that are seen to be growing in problem state, are related to write on a unix domain socket (internal to application). Since the data is not read, the send buffer keeps growing and the associated memory does not gets released. Every telemetry response from the producer does a 1 byte write on this socket and over a period of time the send buffer gets full. The default size of the unix socket send buffer is set to 512MB. But there is no functional impact.

items.synopsis: EVPN next-hop installation for ESI over VTEP fails after remote device restart on PTX and QFX platforms.
items.description: On all Junos Evolved PTX and QFX series platforms, running EVPN (Ethernet Virtual Private Network) and ESI LAG (Ethernet Segment Identifier Link Aggregation Group) is causing issues with the next-hop installation after restarting of remote or peer devices, which affects the overall network stability and performance.

items.synopsis: The snmpwalk for OID ifJnxInputErrors is not working on Junos Evolved platforms
items.description: On Junos Evolved platforms, the snmpwalk for OID ifJnxInputErrors (1.3.6.1.4.1.2636.3.3.1.1.36) is not working. This issue has no impact on traffic.

items.synopsis: on QFX5130, duplicate-mac-detect action discard does not work . The action shutdown port should be used instead.
items.description: When duplicate-mac-detect feature is configured, if the mac moves from leaf to network in a VXLAN enviroment, the action discard does not take effect. The mac move is prevented. As an alternate, use the action shutdown port instead which is also one of the supported options.

items.synopsis: ACX7509 : Evopfemand core triggered RE switchover. Major service impact
items.description: A crash in Broadcom code is leading to evo-pfemand core. RE switchover is triggered due this crash/core.

items.category: Libjtask for RPD tasks, scheduler, timers, memory, and slip
items.synopsis: Memory leak when deactivating/reactivating routing instances with vrf-table-label
items.description: On all Junos Evolved platforms, a memory leak occurs when a routing instance configured with "vrf-table-label" is deactivated and then reactivated, followed by a Routing Engine (RE) switchover on dual RE systems. This issue causes a slow memory leak in the system.

items.category: Packet Based Link Qualification Analysis (PBLQ) on EVO platforms
items.synopsis: Interface failure when removing and adding the ports to ae bundle
items.description: On all Junos Evolved PTX10001-36MR/PTX10001-36MR-K/PTX10008/PTX10016 platforms, removing a port from an Aggregated Ethernet (AE) bundle and then re-adding it causes the interface (IF) to go down and not come back up.

items.category: Issues related to krt-async routing infrastructure
items.synopsis: Undeleted LSI in RPD but deleted in IFMAND
items.description: An LSI IFL remains in RPD even after being deleted by the interface manager daemon. It is visible in show interface routing but not in show interfaces, indicating that RPD still holds the IFL despite its removal elsewhere. rpd-agent does not send a delete message to RPD due to a reference count issue. Another daemon?likely l2ald?still holds a reference to the IFL. rpd-agent only sends the delete once all references are cleared, which doesn't happen in this case. The fix is to send a "delete pending" message from rpd-agent to RPD. RPD will treat this as a delete and remove the IFL, ensuring consistency across the system.

items.synopsis: A few line cards will be stuck in the 'Present' state and later go 'Offline'
items.description: A system equipped with specific line cards, the line cards will be stuck in the 'Present' state and later go 'Offline' after the line card or router is rebooted. Ideally, the Line Card should go 'Online' instead it goes 'Offline'.
